conviction_note: The Q4 quarter is a base-case beat: consensus revenue of $368-373m sits below the $377m guide midpoint, and the guide rests on a Meta deal and minimum volume commitments already in hand. The stock trades on the first FY27 guide, though, and the memory-driven collapse in handset and PC units (IDC -22%/-20% Y/Y, Qualcomm handsets -26%) puts the street's +3.3% FY27 revenue ($1.47B) at risk. Against that, the stock already fell 6.4% in five days on 3x volume with a Rosenblatt target cut, the skew pays for upside (-3.25), and last November a below-street initial guide closed flat. Net: a small negative lean (findings sum -1.3, p_up 47 on an 8.5% absolute move, scaled -0.51). The two numbers agree in sign; the scaled one is smaller because the de-risking and the skew pull p_up toward 50.

next_guide.basis: Three things push the first FY27 guide to or below the street's $1.47B. The memory crisis cut CQ3 handset and PC units about 20% (IDC, Gartner, Qualcomm), and the CFO said on the July call that the longer memory costs persist the more they flow through. FY26 carried a large Q2 recovery and a Q4 lifted by MVC timing. And last November Dolby guided its first quarter well below the street ($315-345m vs $354.5m). Offsets are a full year of Meta VDP, auto Atmos and wearables.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 consensus revenue ($368.4m Zacks/EW, $371.9m Benzinga, $372.76m MarketBeat) sits $4-9m below the $377m guide midpoint. Earnings Whispers says reaching the guide is largely a matter of booking the Meta VDP deal (signed early in the quarter) and MVC timing already in hand. EPS consensus ($1.14-1.19, disputed) sits in the lower half of the $1.13-1.28 guide, and the whisper is $1.26. Expect revenue around $380m, a ~2-3% beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dolby beats EPS most quarters (Q3 FY26 +$0.02, Q4 FY25 $0.99 vs $0.70) and the stock moves on the guide instead. Q4 FY25 beat revenue and EPS, and the stock fell 1.8% premarket on the Q1 guide before closing +0.06%. Q3 FY26 missed revenue consensus and rose +13.6% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the whisper already sits at $1.26. The residual is that the revenue consensus below midpoint is stale relative to a deal signed in the quarter. If priced, the stock would not have sold off 6% into the print.
findings.independence: Company guide and the Meta/MVC drivers: Q3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001308547/000119312526326149/d165402dex991.htm) and the Q3 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/dolby-dlb-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: Memory crisis in Dolby's mobile and PC end markets during its fiscal Q4 (CQ3 2026): IDC has smartphone shipments -22% Y/Y to 255.3m, the largest decline on record, and warns of downside to 2027 (2026-10-15). IDC has PCs -20.1% (2026-10-08), Gartner -22.4% (2026-10-12). Qualcomm's handset revenue fell 26% and its Q1 FY27 profit guide came in light (2026-11-04). Mobile plus PC is roughly a third of Dolby licensing. On the July call the CFO said FY26 mobile was held up only mid-single-digit by MVCs and that the longer memory costs persist, the more they flow through. The FY27 guide carries the risk.
findings.link: Qualcomm implements Dolby Atmos/Vision in Snapdragon handsets, and handset and PC OEMs are Dolby's per-unit licensees. By the Q3 call, mobile (incl. wearables) and PC together are roughly 30-35% of Dolby licensing (share estimated, not stated in the sources).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2026-04-30): a cautious guide with memory flagged, -10.4%. Q3 FY26: a strong Q4 guide, +13.6%. The guide line has carried this stock's two largest recent moves.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's FY27 revenue of $1.47B (+3.3%) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.58 (+6%) still assume growth. If the unit collapse were fully reflected, FY27 revenue consensus would sit at or below FY26's ~$1.425B, and the skew would not be call-bid. Net of the rest of the company: broadcast (~1/3, unaffected), full-year Meta VDP, auto Atmos and wearables have to offset it, which is why this is not sized larger.
findings.independence: Gartner PC data (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-12-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-declined-22-point-4-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2026-as-component-cost-inflation-raised-asps). Qualcomm handset -26% (https://investinglive.com/stocks/qualcomm-beats-q4-forecasts-shares-slip-2-as-profit-guidance-comes-in-light/). Dolby CFO on memory (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/dolby-dlb-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). One driver from several sources, counted once.

findings.finding: This print carries the first FY27 guide, and Dolby guides its first quarter conservatively. Last November it guided Q1 FY26 to $315-345m against $354.5m street (EPS $0.79-0.94 vs $1.02), and the initial FY26 range of $1.39-1.44B was +5% at the midpoint. The FY27 comp includes a large Q2 FY26 recovery and a Q4 lifted by MVC timing. A first FY27 range centred below the street's $1.47B is the likelier outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-18, initial FY guide with Q1 well below street: -1.8% premarket, closed +0.06% (baseline). 2026-04-30, weak next-quarter guide: -10.4%. 2026-07-30, strong next-quarter guide: +13.6%. The market has looked through Dolby's habitual Q1 conservatism, though not through a weak mid-year guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The street FY27 revenue of $1.47B was updated 2026-11-16 and still shows growth. A street that expected conservatism would sit closer to flat. Last year's flat close is why this is sized at -1.0 and not more.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 large-recovery and MVC-timing comments from the Q3 FY26 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/dolby-dlb-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). The initial FY26 range is in https://www.barchart.com/story/news/37307355/dolby-laboratories-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results (raised to $1.40-1.45B in January). Shares the FY27-guide line with the memory finding but rests on different facts (guiding habit and comps, not units).

findings.finding: Mid-quarter: on 2026-09-23 Dolby and Meta expanded Atmos and Vision across Meta's ecosystem. Meta's new AI glasses are the first global consumer device to capture audio in Atmos, and its next VR device will support Vision and Atmos. This is a product-support release with no license terms, but it extends the Meta relationship (already a VDP licensee for Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp) into wearables, a category management named as an FY27 growth driver.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to a product-partnership release found. The Meta VDP license itself was part of the +13.6% Q3 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and largely priced. The residual is whether management quantifies wearables or VDP growth in the FY27 guide, which would show as a guide midpoint above the memory-adjusted street.
findings.independence: Company PDF of the same release (https://s27.q4cdn.com/365963565/files/doc_news/Dolby-and-Meta-Expand-Dolby-Atmos-and-Dolby-Vision-Across-Metas-Ecosystem-2026.pdf). Same document.

findings.finding: Peer InterDigital (Q3 2026, reported 2026-10-29): smartphone licensing revenue -10% Y/Y ($122.6m vs $136.4m), CE/IoT/auto +97% to ~$56m, full-year contracted outlook raised to $813-819m on new agreements, with $36.2m of catch-up revenue. This is a mixed read: licensing deals keep signing while phone-linked revenue shrinks.
findings.link: Both license video-codec and media patents to smartphone and TV OEMs (HEVC/VVC pools such as Access Advance overlap Dolby's imaging patents). IDCC's smartphone deals are mostly fixed-fee, so it is less unit-sensitive than Dolby's per-unit royalties.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No DLB reaction to IDCC prints found.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and has offsetting signs, so it sits at 0. A different fee structure limits transmission.

findings.finding: Peer Adeia (Q3 2026, reported 2026-11-02) cut its 2026 revenue outlook to $375-415m from $395-435m because large, legally complex media license deals slipped. Q3 media revenue was $65m. Management said the pipeline is unchanged.
findings.link: Adeia licenses media and video IP to pay-TV operators and streamers. Dolby's Video Distribution Program licenses imaging patents to streamers (Meta, Peacock). Customers overlap but no figure was found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No DLB reaction to ADEA prints found.
findings.why_not_priced: Deal-timing slippage at a streamer-IP licensor hints at lumpy timing for Dolby's VDP signings into FY27. That is a weak, unlinked read and sized small.

findings.finding: Capital return: in July the board raised the buyback authorization by $350m to ~$427m remaining. Dolby repurchased ~$65m (1.2m shares) in Q3, and the CFO's policy is to at least offset dilution. With the stock ~10% below its post-Q3 level, the Q4 repurchase count and any FY27 return framework give modest support.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dolby's buyback updates are routine and have not been the reacting line in the baseline prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public. The residual is the pace, and a stepped-up Q4 repurchase would show in the share count.
findings.independence: CFO buyback policy on the Q3 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/dolby-dlb-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

baseline_tension: The guide-risk findings lean negative, against a call-bid skew (-3.25). The 6.4% pre-print slide suggests part of that risk is already in the price, so p_up moves only to 47 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): EPS consensus is disputed ($1.14 vs $1.19), so the consensus_bar finding was trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6. Revenue rests on the company guide plus agreeing estimates.

Rule 9 and rule 5 (segment net of the rest, proxy): the memory finding was cut from -2.0 to -1.5. Mobile+PC is about a third of licensing, and broadcast, Meta VDP and auto offset it. Transmission is partly company-confirmed (CFO July call) but FY27 is inferred.
Rule 1 (reaction function): the next-guide finding was cut from -1.5 to -1.0 because the stock closed flat last November on a below-street initial guide.
Rule 7 (skew): negatives run against a call-bid skew and a moderate, uncrowded short, so p_up moved from 45 to 47.
